div.p: XPath 4.0 path expressions can navigate JSON - maps and arrays - as they do XML. The jtree() function wraps a map or array in a tree of JNodes, with a JNode for each map entry and array member, so a path such as $order/customer/name works on JSON data, with predicates, the descendant and parent axes, and the other features of path expressions.

When a JNode is declared with a record type, for example jnode(*, order), the XSLT/XPath extension knows which fields each step can reach. It checks each step, offers the field names as auto-completion suggestions, and shows each field's type and documentation on hover.

JNodes need version="4.0" and Saxon-PE or Saxon-EE 13, run with syntax extensions enabled (Quick Run enables these for a version="4.0" stylesheet). Saxon-HE 13 doesn't support XPath 4.0 syntax. In an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet, the jnode(...) item type and the get(...) node test are reported as needing XPath 4.0.
div.aside: A sample project, xslt-json-schema-records, shows the features on this page in use. It converts a JSON Schema to XSLT 4.0 record types, reading the schema as JNodes, then reads JSON order data typed with the generated record types.
div.p: A JNode tree is made with jtree(), from a map or array - for example the result of json-doc() or parse-json():

ul.li: Name steps select map entries by key, e.g. $order/customer/name. * selects every entry of a map, or every member of an array, e.g. $order/lines/*.

get(...) is the node test for a key that isn't an NCName, such as get('$ref') or get('first name'), or for an array member by position, such as get(1). The extension reports get('a') used on its own, as a function call, as a call to an unknown function.
Axes work as they do for XML: $schema//get('$ref') finds every $ref at any depth, and $line/../../currency goes up from an order line, through the lines array, to the order.

jkey() gives a JNode's key - the map key, or the position of an array member - and jvalue() gives the value it wraps. Where a value is atomized, such as in an arithmetic expression or a text value template, a JNode gives its value, so $line/quantity * $line/unit-price works without jvalue().
A JNode is matched with the jnode() item type, e.g. $tree/type instance of jnode(type). jnode() is offered in auto-completion for as attributes in XSLT 4.0.

div.aside: Saxon 13 doesn't support type node tests such as ~record(...) or ~xs:string in a path step, so the extension reports these as errors.
div.p: A variable, parameter or function result declared as jnode(*, T), where T is a record type, is a JNode whose value is a T. A named item type can be used too, e.g. <xsl:item-type name="order-node" as="jnode(*, order)"/>. Child steps from the JNode are then auto-completed and checked against the record's fields, at any depth:
div.code: <xsl:variable name="order-value" as="order" select="json-doc($order-uri)"/> <xsl:variable name="order" as="jnode(*, order)" select="jtree($order-value)"/> ... <xsl:function name="ord:line-total" as="xs:double"> <xsl:param name="line" as="jnode(*, line)"/> <xsl:sequence select="$line/quantity * $line/unit-price"/> </xsl:function>

ul.li: Auto-completion - after a /, the suggestions list the record's fields. Typing $order/customer/ lists the fields of the customer record type.

Checks - a step that isn't a field is a warning, e.g. Child step 'nam' - this is not a field of the record type: customer for $order/customer/nam. A ? lookup on the JNode, e.g. $order?id, is checked in the same way.

Hover - hovering over a field name in a step, such as unit-price in $line/unit-price, shows the field's type. Its @field text is shown too, from the xsl:item-type's documentation note. Hovering over the type name in jnode(*, order) shows the record type, with its fields and documentation.

div.p: Child steps after jtree($p)/, where $p has a record type, are auto-completed and checked in the same way.

figcaption.i: Hovering on order in jnode(*, order) shows the record type, imported from a module of types generated from a JSON Schema: its fields, their types, and each field's description from the schema.

div.p: A / step needs a JNode on its left, not a map. Saxon 13 reports XPTY0019 for a step such as $order-value/id, where $order-value is a map with a record type, so the extension reports this as an error, with the suggested fix jtree($order-value)/id. Alternatives are a lookup, $order-value?id, or a variable declared as a jnode(*, order), as above. A step after a lookup, such as $p?address/city, is reported in the same way.

The xdm:debug() function shows a JNode's location in its tree, as an XPath path from the tree's root, above the value it wraps - in the same way it shows the location of an XML node. For an order line, this is a path such as /lines/*[2], so you can see which part of the JSON each value came from:

The xdm:debug variables auto-completion for xsl:message inserts a call like this one, with every in-scope variable. See Debugging.
div.h3: Things to know about JNodes and record types in Saxon 13

ul.li: A jnode(*, T) type matches only an instance of T. A map with keys that T doesn't declare isn't an instance, so jtree(json-doc('order.json')) doesn't match jnode(*, order) when the data has extra properties. Converting the value to the record type first - as for $order-value above - drops the extra keys, at every depth, and fails if a required field is missing or has the wrong type.

No recursive item types. An xsl:item-type can't refer to itself, directly or through other types (Saxon reports SXTA0001). A field that would refer back, such as a bundle of order lines within an order line, has to be map(*) or array(map(*)) instead, so the steps after it aren't checked.

JSON numbers are xs:double. json-doc() and parse-json() give every JSON number as an xs:double, so a record field for a number must be xs:double - xs:integer would reject the data. A JSON null is an empty sequence, so a nullable field needs an occurrence indicator, e.g. xs:string?.
No ?? operator. Saxon 13 doesn't support the deep lookup operator, so use the descendant axis on JNodes instead, e.g. $schema//get('$ref').

div.h3: Sample: JSON Schema to record types
div.p: The xslt-json-schema-records sample works in two stages:

ol.li: schema-to-records.xsl reads a JSON Schema, order.schema.json, as JNodes, and writes order-types.xsl: an xsl:item-type for the schema and for each of its $defs. Each property's description becomes an @field in the type's documentation note, so it's shown on hover.
order-report.xsl includes order-types.xsl, and prints a summary of order.json, using jnode(*, order), jnode(*, line) and other typed JNodes.

ul.li: typing $order/customer/ to see the customer's fields as suggestions
changing $order/customer/name to $order/customer/nam, to see the warning
hovering on unit-price in $line/unit-price, or on line in jnode(*, line), to see the documentation taken from the schema
changing $order/id to $order-value/id, to see the jtree() error and its fix
adding a property to customer in order.schema.json, running schema-to-records.xsl again, and seeing it offered after $order/customer/

div.p: The sample's README describes how each JSON Schema keyword maps to an XPath type.
